- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak or use lagged sentiment to dampen.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct — apply downward bias in subsequent periods if sentiment weakens.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use 14-day moving average of history to smooth forecast baseline.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend — align forecast to sentiment median rather than peak.
